EnvironmentHelp: doctor checks local configuration. Build and run a project to verify the complete toolchain. Stop the app before rebuilding.
ThemeHelp: Choose a light or dark appearance.
AboutDescription: An interactive guide to XamlNexus tooling, framework behavior and generated source.
DataDescription: Save local records, create and restore database backups, and verify persistence across application restarts.
DataTry: Save a key/value pair, select it to edit, then create a backup. Restoring a backup replaces database contents and asks for confirmation.
DataState: The complete write, query and recovery path
DataStateHelp: The data page separates UI actions, EF Core contexts and database maintenance. Every operation creates its own context and queries again afterward so the UI reflects the final database state.
LifetimeDescription: Edit a page draft, leave it and return to compare recreation of a regular ArcPage with reuse of a [KeepAlive] page.
BackupHelp: Create a snapshot before making changes. Restore replaces the saved database after confirmation.
NavigationRequiredHelp: In your application, derive the page from ArcPage, add [KeepAlive], and enter and leave through XamlNexus navigation, such as ArcNavigationContentView.Navigate. Navigation manages page retention and reuse; the attribute alone does not cache pages you create or replace manually.
RetentionInstructions: Use the switch to choose a page strategy. Enter a title and notes, and optionally enable Loading. Leave and return: a regular page gets a new instance, while a KeepAlive page restores the draft and Loading state.
RetentionAwayHelp: The draft page has left the navigation foreground. Select Return to draft above to continue the flow.
NavigationUsage: KeepAlive preserves the page and the objects it owns: UI controls, animation objects, input and selection state, and ViewModel data such as loaded results and filter conditions. Animation playback, pausing and resuming remain controlled by your animation logic and navigation lifecycle callbacks. A separately retained ViewModel can preserve data even when the page itself is recreated.
RetentionDemoTitle: Leave a draft page, then return
RegularOutcome: Regular page: recreated on return. Input, count and Loading visibility reset; the control ID changes.
CachedOutcome: KeepAlive page: reuses the page, ViewModel and Loading control. Input, count and the enabled spinner remain.
RetentionScope: This compares in-memory state within the running app. Restarting the app clears it.
RetentionBoundaries: What is retained and when not to retain it
FrameworkSourceHelp: Read the actual WinUI template source, bundled for offline browsing. Gallery has its own window appearance; the source below describes the generated application.
WindowDescription: ArcWindow is the generated app's main-window base class, combining the custom title bar, theme material, page host and window-scoped state.
WindowIntro: MainWindow initializes its XAML and supplies ContentHost, Key and IsMainWindow. It then calls InitializeWindow to connect that visual host to ArcWindow services.
WindowDetail1: ArcWindowHost combines the title bar, navigation content region and theme-transition layer. When custom title bars are supported, ArcWindow connects the drag region while retaining system minimize, maximize and close buttons. Business pages only need to occupy the content region.
WindowDetail2: The main window applies light, dark or system theme and keeps Mica or Acrylic aligned with the content theme. A theme change captures the current surface and fades it into the new theme to avoid an abrupt whole-window flash. Try theme changes in Gallery settings; backdrop changes require restart in this sample.
WindowDetail3: Windows that need application-wide coordination register a Key with ArcWindowManager. The app can find the main or another active window and post window-scoped feedback. A real close detaches events, and closing the main window also releases shared window and theme state.
PageDescription: ArcPage is the navigable page base class: receive parameters through Payload, organize work with lifecycle callbacks, and coordinate tasks with Loading before leaving.
PageIntro: ArcNavigationContentView manages pages in the current host by ArcType. Navigation must go through ArcNavigate for lifecycle callbacks, Payload merging and KeepAlive reuse to work together.
PageDetail1: Navigation passes a FrameworkPayload to OnEnter. Keep page layout in XAML, and use the entry callback to read navigation context and start the work needed by that page.
PageDetail2: Read parameters and start page work in OnEnter. Stop interaction and wait for required page tasks in OnPreLeaveAsync. A regular page then uses OnLeaveAsync to cancel subscriptions and requests and OnDestroy to release its page context. OnDestroy is navigation cleanup, not a .NET garbage-collection notification.
PageDetail3: With [KeepAlive], navigation retains the page instance and its owned controls, animation objects and ViewModel data. Returning reuses that instance. Animation playback remains application-controlled, and restoring state after exit requires persistence.
RecentEmpty: Open a sample to see your recent visits here during this session.

WindowFlowTitle: From MainWindow construction to an interactive window
WindowNode1: 1. Construction: ArcWindow reads theme and backdrop preferences and subscribes to Activated and AppWindow.Closing.
WindowNode2: 2. Initialization: InitializeWindow registers AppRoot.Loaded, tracks the window, then sets startup position, system backdrop and extended title bar.
WindowNode3: 3. Loaded: ArcWindow obtains the Compositor and applies the theme. Later theme changes capture the current UI, apply the new theme and fade out the snapshot.
WindowFlowHelp: Activation keeps title-bar visuals in sync. A real AppWindow close detaches events and clears shared main-window state; hiding the window or cancelling close does not run that cleanup path.
PageFlowTitle: The actual order of one ArcNavigate call
PageNode1: 1. Resolve the target: prefer a background page in the current host; for a [KeepAlive] type, then query ArcPageContextManager; otherwise create a new instance.
PageNode2: 2. Enter the target: merge Payload, add the page to PageMap and the visual tree, then call NavigateEnter → OnEnter. Play the enter transition when configured.
PageNode3: 3. Exit the previous page: call NavigateExit → OnPreLeaveAsync and wait for Loading blockers. A regular page is then removed from PageMap and the visual tree, runs OnLeaveAsync and OnDestroy, and finally lets the target become Active.
PageFlowHelp: The target enters before the previous page finishes its asynchronous exit. If rapid navigation makes the old page PreActive or Active again, the removal callback keeps it in the visual tree.
WindowExampleHelp: Minimal window structure for a generated WinUI project. Replace MyApp with your project namespace; retain existing dependency injection and startup wiring when adapting your generated MainWindow.
PageExampleHelp: Create a DetailsPage and navigate to it from your window. The XAML page and C# class belong in separate files. The navigation container declaration belongs inside the window content host.

HomeLead: Build with WinUI 3. Start with navigation, MVVM and services already connected, then compose the capabilities your application needs.
HomeConsoleHelp: After installing the tool and checking your environment, run these commands in a terminal.
HomeHighlightsHelp: See what the generated project already provides, which Recipes can be added, and how the project can be checked and upgraded later.
Highlight1Title: Start with the plumbing in place
Highlight1Body: Navigation, MVVM, dependency injection, configuration and logging arrive together. Start writing your page and application logic.
Highlight2Body: Choose a starting profile and add settings, SQLite, a tray or update support through Recipes.
Highlight3Body: Preview supported changes, inspect project health and upgrade scaffold infrastructure with conflict reporting.
HomeSamplesHelp: Try scenarios for windows and navigation, lists and storage, then inspect their source and integration steps.
HomeRouteHelp: Follow the development workflow into the relevant guidance and interactive sample.
Route1Body: Install, check prerequisites and run your first project.
Route2Body: Start a business page from a blank, list, details or form template.
Route3Body: Add Recipes as needed, then maintain the project with status and upgrade commands.
ToolGuideIntro: Work through four tasks: create a project, scaffold pages, add Recipes and maintain the result. Each section shows commands, result examples, source templates and usage boundaries. Installed versions can differ; verify with xamlnexus --help.
PageTemplatesIntro: Choose a template by page responsibility
PageTemplatesHelp: Choose a page responsibility, try its preview, then inspect the generated files, runtime flow and actual source used by the CLI.
PageTemplateBlankBody: An ArcPage, title and empty ViewModel for pages with custom layouts and little predefined state.
PageTemplateListBody: Includes search, refresh, loading, empty results, error recovery and stale-request rejection for browsing collections.
PageTemplateListFlow: Search or refresh → request → map UI state → cancel on leave
PageTemplateDetailsBody: Reads an id from FrameworkPayload, loads one record, and handles loading, retry and cancellation when the page is left.
PageTemplateDetailsFlow: Read id → load → show record or retry → cancel on leave
PageTemplateFormBody: Creates a record without an id or loads one for editing, including validation, unsaved-change feedback, save and reset.
PageTemplateFormFlow: Load draft → edit and validate → save → replace original snapshot
BlankPreviewBody: This is the business content area. The blank template only wires the page and ViewModel.
ListTemplatePreviewBody: The list template already has a complete example where you can try search, refresh, failure and retry.
DetailsFailureHint: Enter retry: the first request fails and retry succeeds.
DetailsErrorMessage: The first sample request failed. Keep the id and retry to recover.
DetailsResultDescription: The record was loaded from the navigation payload. Replace the sample data source with an application service.
PageTemplateBoundary: These templates provide runnable UI states and replaceable data-source contracts. They do not infer business fields, database models or APIs. Details and form pages use the payload id to select a record.
DetailsTemplateDescription: The actual CLI details template. Replace project and page names, then copy the complete source.
FormTemplateDescription: The actual CLI form template. Replace project and page names, then copy the complete source.
ArchitectureIntro: Choose the runtime architecture, then the initial capability set.
ArchitectureHelp: preset selects pure WinUI or a Hybrid host, while profile selects standard or basic. The default is winui + standard.
WinuiBody: A WinUI application entry point with shared models and services. Choose this for a straightforward native desktop application.
HybridBody: A WinUI frontend with a WPF background host. Host-side capabilities and frontend communication have explicit boundaries; business RPC methods remain yours to implement.
StandardBody: The default profile includes the settings interface with theme and language controls, on top of the shared application infrastructure.
BasicBody: Omits the full settings interface, while retaining navigation, configuration, logging, theme and localization foundations. Add settings later when needed.
ProjectMapTitle: Project structure and code entry points
ProjectMapBody:
UI → application entry and window composition
MainPanel → pages and ViewModels
UIComponent → shared UI and ArcXaml foundations
Models / Common → contracts, configuration and shared services
Recipe projects → additional capabilities, such as Data for SQLite
RecipesIntro: Five built-in Recipes, added when you need them.
RecipesHelp: Use recipes to inspect built-in components and their support boundaries, and list to inspect capabilities installed in the current project. Review the file plan with --dry-run before applying it.
RecipeSettingsBody: WinUI + hybrid · Optional for basic; included in standard. Adds the settings panel and navigation integration.
RecipeSqliteBody: WinUI + hybrid · Adds an EF Core SQLite data project. In hybrid projects, data access belongs to the host. Connect your own business models and services.
RecipeTrayBody: Pure WinUI · Tray menu, show/hide, exit and balloon notifications. Hybrid projects already include tray infrastructure.
RecipeUpdaterBody: Pure WinUI · Depends on settings. Adds an HTTPS update client and verified downloads; configure your own update source. Hybrid includes update infrastructure.
RecipeEditorBody: WinUI + hybrid · Adds an .editorconfig to make formatting conventions explicit in your generated workspace.
RecipeBoundary: The Gallery data page includes custom CRUD, backup and restore demonstrations. These screens are not generated by adding the SQLite Recipe.
MaintenanceIntro: Inspect project status, then update Recipes or the project scaffold separately.
MaintenanceHelp: Run commands from the project directory or pass --project explicitly. The Gallery only displays commands; use --dry-run first for commands that modify the project.
MaintainInspectBody: doctor --environment checks prerequisites before creation. In a project, status summarizes scaffold and Recipe versions, structural validation and diagnostics, then suggests the next maintenance command. Use validate and doctor for the individual findings. Follow with a real build and launch.
MaintainComponentBody: update --all finds every installed Recipe with a newer bundled version, rehearses the complete update in a temporary project copy, then commits it as one transaction. Updating or removing stops when tracked files have changed or are missing so you can review those edits first.
UpdateAllFlowTitle: Three stages of one batch update
UpdateAllFlowDiscover: 01 Discover · Compare installed versions with Recipes bundled in this tool.
UpdateAllFlowRehearse: 02 Rehearse · Apply every update to a temporary project copy and validate the result.
UpdateAllFlowCommit: 03 Commit once · Recheck manifest and file hashes, then write the combined change; failure leaves no partial update.
MaintainScaffoldBody: upgrade uses the generation baseline to merge managed infrastructure. Changes that cannot be merged reliably become conflicts; export them, resolve the .merge files and apply with --resolve-from.
UpdateBoundary: Three different updates: dotnet tool update upgrades the CLI; update <id> upgrades a Recipe; upgrade evolves project infrastructure. --json formats output and does not make an operation read-only.
GuideStep1Body: Use Windows with a .NET 8 / WinUI development environment. Install the tool once; use dotnet tool update --global XamlNexus if it is already installed.
GuideStep2Body: Creates the default WinUI + standard project. run builds and launches Debug / x64 / unpackaged output. Stop with Ctrl+C before editing; run does not provide watch or hot reload.
GuideStep3Body: Edit MyApp.MainPanel/MainPage.xaml and ViewModels/MainViewModel.cs, then preview and generate a list page as the first business page. Try the details and form variants under Tool guide / Page templates.
GuideStep4Title: 04 / Add storage and inspect the project
GuideStep4Body: Review the SQLite file plan with --dry-run, apply the Recipe, then check the project with validate, doctor and status. The storage component provides a data layer; you still design the data model and business UI.
GuideNext: Continue with architectures, Recipes and project maintenance
GuideCodeNote: Commands are copyable examples. The Gallery does not execute them.
FooterBody: Browse the Wiki for full walkthroughs, or inspect the implementation on GitHub.
WindowDemoHelp: Resize or maximize the window first and observe how the title bar and navigation region adapt together. Then switch theme in appearance settings and confirm that title bar, backdrop and page content update as one window surface.
WindowAnatomyTitle: Three responsibilities in an application window
WindowAnatomyBody:
Title bar: dragging, system buttons and application actions.
Content host: navigation and the current page.
Window lifecycle: registration, activation and cleanup on close.
WindowUseHelp: A generated project already contains a working MainWindow. Most business pages never need window APIs. Edit MainWindow and ArcWindowHost only for title-bar content, startup placement, backdrop, multiple windows or window-scoped messages.
PageDemoTitle: Pass data while opening a page
PageDemoHelp: Enter a message and navigate. The sample creates a FrameworkPayload and the target ArcPage reads it in OnEnter. Use this pattern for a record id, filter or presentation mode needed by this navigation.
PageDemoPlaceholder: Enter a message and navigate to show the target page here.
PageUseHelp: Derive pages that participate in navigation lifecycle from ArcPage and provide a unique ArcType. The sender navigates with ArcNavigationContentView.ArcNavigate, and the target reads FrameworkPayload in OnEnter.
RetentionUseHelp: Use [KeepAlive] on an ArcPage and enter it through the XamlNexus navigation container. The container reuses the page instance on return. Decide separately which data needs saving across application restarts.
ListTrySteps: Search for WinUI, then enter an unmatched term to see the empty state. Enable Slow request or Simulate failure and refresh to observe loading, errors and retry.
ListScopeHelp: The sample uses three in-memory records to demonstrate page states. In a generated page, replace IProjectsDataSource with your application data source.
ListBehaviorTitle: UI states produced by one request
ListBehaviorBody: The ViewModel owns request state and visible data. IProjectsDataSource only returns raw data asynchronously, while bindings select the loading, error, empty or list presentation.
WindowDetail4: Key identifies a window in ArcWindowManager. MainWindow, ActiveWindows and GetArcWindow(key) locate windows; IsNeedTrack controls registration and IsActive reports activation. A temporary window that never needs global lookup can remain untracked.
WindowDetail5: AppNavView exposes the top-level NavigationView and ContentHost provides the page content region. InfobarMessages is a shared window-level message collection for feedback such as update results or connection failures that does not belong to one page.
WindowDetail6: The default places the window in the center of the current display work area. Override SetWindowStartupPosition to restore a previous location or apply business-specific placement. WindowEx and AppWindow provide sizing and display operations. Cleanup runs only after a real close; hiding to tray or cancelling close keeps the instance alive.
PageDetail4: Wrap page content in ArcPageHost and attach its LoadingControlHost to ArcContext after page initialization. RunAsync is for work without measurable progress; RunWithProgressAsync updates progress through report(current, total). A CancellationTokenSource shows a cancel action, but the business operation must still observe the token.
PageDetail5: A Loading operation registers a page blocker in ArcContext. When navigation leaves, the page stops interaction and waits for registered work before deciding whether to retain the instance or clean it up. Both regular and KeepAlive pages wait, so Loading coordinates tasks while retention controls instance reuse.
PageDetail6: ArcType identifies the page type and its page context. A regular page type is managed as one instance. Enable multiple-instance mode when the same page type must display independent content simultaneously, but those instances cannot rely on shared type-based context lookup.
PayloadTitle: Navigation payload: data needed to open this page
PayloadHelp: FrameworkPayload stores typed values under string or NaviPayloadKey keys. The sender writes with Set. The target should prefer TryGet<T> for optional values and use Get<T> only when the value must exist. Payload is suitable for a record id or filter, not durable state. A retained page keeps its old Payload, and current merge behavior preserves old values for duplicate keys; use a shared ViewModel or an explicit update method for continuously changing data.
LoadingUsageTitle: Loading: one place for tasks, progress and cancellation
LoadingUsageHelp: Attach the loading host after InitializeComponent and start work from the UI thread. Business operations own cancellation and error handling, and one page loading context should not run overlapping operations. Navigation waits for registered work to release, so long-lived background work that does not belong to a page should run in a separate service.
LoadingRetentionTitle: Retain Loading along with the page
LoadingRetentionHelp: Enable Loading, leave the sample page and return to the same mode. A KeepAlive page keeps the same Loading control and its visible state; a regular page creates a new control. Compare the control ID as well as the spinner. Retaining the animation object does not guarantee an exact animation frame across hiding or unloading.
LoadingDemoScope: This is the framework Loading control. The toggle demonstrates UI/animation retention without running a background request. For task lifetime, progress and cancellation, see the ArcPage Loading examples.
PageLifecycleTitle: Entering, leaving and finishing page work
DemoFailureMessage: Simulated failure. Uncheck the option and refresh to retry.
ToolGuideDescription: Create and run projects, scaffold pages, add Recipes, and maintain generated applications with diagnostics and upgrades.
NavigationFundamentalsDescription: Move from the application window into page navigation: see how ArcWindow hosts the title bar and content, then use ArcPage for payloads, lifecycle and retention.
NavigationCapabilitiesDescription: Explore two complete data-page examples: an async list covers loading, empty and failure states, while SQLite covers persistence, backup and restore.
WindowDetailsIntro: Generated projects already contain the basic wiring. You normally use these APIs directly only when changing the window shell, appearance transitions or multi-window behavior.
PageDetailsIntro: Navigation payloads, Loading and lifecycle can be used independently. Page retention builds on the same navigation lifecycle. Expand the capability you need for its usage and boundaries.
RetentionDetailsIntro: Retention means reusing the same page instance. The lifecycle log below shows what differs between a regular and KeepAlive page when leaving and returning.
ListDetailsIntro: The key behavior is how one request updates IsBusy, HasError, Items and IsEmpty, and how leaving the page prevents stale results from writing back to the UI.
DataDetailsIntro: This sample separates page actions, EF Core contexts and database maintenance. The steps below trace one save, one refresh and one restore.
WindowImplementationTitle: Three groups of window capabilities managed by ArcWindow
ListImplementationTitle: How one list request drives the UI
DataImplementationTitle: How SQLite data is written, queried and restored
RetentionResolutionTitle: Why the page instance is reused
RetentionResolutionBody: On return, the navigation host first looks for a reusable background page. A [KeepAlive] page can also recover its original instance from page context. A regular page is recreated when no reusable instance exists, so its id changes.
RetentionLifecycleTitle: What happens when the page is left
RetentionLifecycleBody: Every page first stops interaction and waits for Loading work in OnPreLeaveAsync. A regular page then runs cleanup. A KeepAlive page remains in the host as an invisible background page and runs OnEnter again on return.
RetentionStateBody: Page fields, input, selection, a page-owned ViewModel, animation objects and the Loading control remain with the instance. This memory state disappears when the app exits; durable data belongs in settings, files or a database.
ListRequestFlowBody: The first visit or Refresh shows progress and prevents the same request from running twice. A new request also clears the previous error.
ListUiStateBody: A successful request shows the list; no matching rows shows the empty state. Search filters loaded data without calling the data source again.
ListCancellationBody: A failure shows its reason and allows another refresh. Leaving cancels the current request, and a result that arrives later cannot overwrite the page that was left.
DataWriteFlowBody: Save creates an independent AppDbContext through IDbContextFactory and looks up the record by Key. It updates Value and timestamp when found, or adds a record, then calls SaveChangesAsync. Delete uses ExecuteDeleteAsync for the selected Key. Both paths query again afterward instead of assuming the UI cache matches the database.
DataQueryFlowBody: Refresh creates a new context and queries AppState with AsNoTracking so the page does not retain tracked entities. The order preference is written to the settings service, and changing it runs the query again. Entries is only the current query result; the SQLite file is the source that survives pages and process restarts.
DataRecoveryFlowBody: Integrity runs SQLite integrity_check. Backup uses SQLite BackupDatabase to write a temporary file and moves it into the Backups directory only after the write succeeds. Restore first opens the candidate read-only, checks integrity and migration compatibility, and performs a test query. Only then does it create a before-restore safety copy, replace the current database and query the page again.
WindowPurposeBody: ArcWindow manages the entire desktop window rather than one business page. Use it for a consistent title bar, theme backdrop, startup placement, window-level feedback or multi-window lookup. Forms, lists and loading state inside a page still belong to ArcPage or a business ViewModel.
WindowBoundaryTitle: What the framework and application each own
WindowBoundaryBody: ArcWindow owns the window shell, system window events and shared window state. The application chooses title-bar actions, which windows are tracked, whether close hides to tray, and which business pages appear in the content region.
PagePurposeBody: Derive from ArcPage when content receives navigation data, starts and stops work on entry and exit, uses coordinated Loading, or retains its instance when revisited. Content that only forms part of another page and has no independent navigation lifecycle is better represented by a UserControl.
PageBoundaryTitle: Page lifecycle is not business-data lifecycle
PageBoundaryBody: ArcPage coordinates the current page surface and its work; it does not persist data. Put cross-page state in a service or shared ViewModel, and store state needed after application restart in settings, files or a database.
RetentionPurposeTitle: When page retention is worth using
RetentionPurposeBody: Retain temporary state users expect when returning, such as an unfinished form, list scroll position, filters or expensive UI objects. Do not rely on [KeepAlive] when page instances can grow without bound, data must survive application restart, or work should continue independently of a page.
RetentionCostBody: A retained page keeps its controls, ViewModel and referenced objects in memory. Enable it for a small number of frequently revisited pages whose state has clear value. For many detail pages, save the necessary state and allow the page to be recreated.
RecipePlanHelp: add accepts comma-separated Recipe ids for one batch. The tool validates the project, resolves dependencies, preset restrictions and conflicts, skips installed components, then applies the whole file set as one transaction. Use --dry-run to inspect the complete plan first.
CommandsIntro: Everyday commands from creation to automation
CommandsHelp: These examples cover options and execution boundaries beyond the quick start. Each line in a code block is an independent example; combine it with the path and options for your project.
CommandCreateBody: Running xamlnexus alone collects configuration in an interactive terminal; new is the reproducible command form. preset selects winui or hybrid, profile selects standard or basic, and features installs Recipes during creation. You can also choose the parent output directory, generated app language and sln or slnx format.
CommandPageBody: page add offers blank, list, details and form. blank is a basic ArcPage; list wires async collection states; details reads a navigation id and handles loading, retry and cancellation; form supports create/edit, validation, dirty state, async save and reset. All four register navigation by default. Use --no-navigation for embedded content and --dry-run to inspect the files.
CommandRunBody: run starts a Debug, x64, unpackaged application. A hybrid project starts its host, which then opens the UI. --dry-run prints the launch plan and --no-build reuses existing output. Ctrl+C stops the process; the command does not provide watch or hot reload.
CommandAutomationBody: status, list, validate, doctor, Recipe changes and upgrade support --json. status is a useful CI maintenance entry point: it returns 1 when structure or diagnostics are unhealthy and reports scaffold and Recipe version states separately. Exit code 2 means invalid usage; cancelling run with Ctrl+C returns 130. Pass --project explicitly to avoid resolving the wrong directory.
CommandGalleryTitle: Open the Gallery matching the CLI version
CommandGalleryBody: gallery downloads the Windows x64 package from the release manifest, verifies it, caches it under local application data and starts it. It currently requires Windows 10 1809 or later. A source build without a release manifest should build samples/XamlNexus.Gallery directly. Close an existing Gallery window before opening another version.
CommandBoundary: --dry-run previews without changing project files. --json changes the output format and does not make a mutating command read-only. upgrade --conflict-output writes conflict artifacts, so it cannot be combined with --dry-run.
WindowLiveHelp: The values below come from the running Gallery windows. A new ArcWindow remains open when you navigate away and closes only when you close it or exit the main window. Refresh after changing window focus.
WindowStatusUnavailable: The current element is not attached to an ArcWindow yet.
WindowSetupTitle: Define MainWindow and its content host
WindowCompositionSummary: ArcWindowHost combines the custom title bar, navigation content and theme transition layer. InitializeWindow wires window tracking, startup placement and the title bar.
WindowAppearanceSummary: The window synchronizes theme, Mica or Acrylic and title-bar state. Theme changes fade out a snapshot of the current surface.
WindowCoordinationSummary: Key locates tracked windows. ContentHost and AppNavView expose page hosting, while InfobarMessages carries window-level feedback.
LoadingInteractiveHelp: Run indeterminate or progress Loading. The overlay blocks the content below; the progress example can also be stopped with the cancel button in the overlay.
LoadingDemoContent: This area represents page content while data is being loaded.
PageLifecycleShortHelp: Both pages wait for Loading work to finish. A regular page then runs cleanup, while a KeepAlive page stays in the navigation host until it is entered again.
RetentionModeHeader: What happens when the page is revisited
RetentionObserveHelp: Watch the draft content and Loading state, then compare the Page, ViewModel and Loading instance identifiers at the bottom.
ListCancellationCode: HasError  →  InfoBar    |    Cancel  →  reject late result
SecondaryWindowHelp: InitializeWindow registers this window with ArcWindowManager. Closing it removes its key from the window list on the original page.
PageOnEnterTitle: OnEnter · Enter or reactivate the page
PageOnEnterDetail:
When: every entry through ArcNavigate, including a retained page returning to the foreground.
Use it for: reading FrameworkPayload, selecting a record, refreshing stale data and resuming page interaction.
Requirement: call base.OnEnter(payload) first. The same KeepAlive instance may enter repeatedly, so avoid duplicate event subscriptions or collection entries.
PageOnPreLeaveDetail:
When: every navigation away, for both regular and KeepAlive pages. The framework hides the page, disables input and waits for every task registered with KeepAliveBlocking.
Use it for: stop accepting input, cancel requests owned by the page, then await base.OnPreLeaveAsync() so Loading and custom delayed work can finish.
Do not start an unbounded background operation here. Register work when that operation starts.
PageOnLeaveTitle: OnLeaveAsync · Async cleanup for regular pages
PageOnLeaveDetail:
When: after OnPreLeaveAsync, only for a regular page. A KeepAlive page skips this stage during normal navigation. The page is already out of the foreground and OnDestroy follows.
Use it for: await page-owned requests, detach asynchronous subscriptions or commit a short operation that must complete before final cleanup. Do not rely on visible or interactive UI here.
PageOnDestroyDetail:
When: after a regular page finishes leaving, or when the page is actually unloaded from the visual tree. The framework clears Payload and DataContext, unregisters ArcPageContext and sets Stopped.
Use it for: releasing handles, timers and final subscriptions. This is synchronous, so do not start fire-and-forget cleanup. Make custom cleanup idempotent and call base.OnDestroy() last.
PageBlockingTitle: Wait for Loading and custom delayed work
PageBlockingDetail: LoadingContext.RunAsync and RunWithProgressAsync call KeepAliveBlocking.Block() automatically. A custom save, export or animation-finishing task can acquire its own handle when it starts. OnPreLeaveAsync waits for every handle; after the final handle is disposed, a regular page continues to OnLeaveAsync and OnDestroy. Parallel tasks can register separate handles.
PageBlockingWarning: Always release the handle with using or finally, or page leaving will wait forever. A blocker delays page cleanup; it does not cancel work or persist state after the application exits. Long-running independent work belongs in an application service.
